input: board is a rectangular R by C array of one-character ASCII letters; word is an ASCII-letter string of length L. Empty outer/zero-column boards and empty word are accepted. Total R * C is within the shared collection-size bound; no caller changes occur during traversal. All input collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections; node fields, where present, are plain data fields. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Every individual collection length, computed storage count and index fits [0, 4294967295], except explicit -1 sentinels. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Actual allocation/resource capacity and completion remain qualification obligations, not guarantees from these declared bounds. JavaScript integers are primitive safe-integer Number values, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt.
return: Boolean indicating whether word can be formed by a cardinally adjacent path without reusing any board cell. Empty word returns true; a nonempty word on an empty board returns false.
mutation_aliasing: Neither board, any row, nor word is changed. Visited flags are private and undone when a DFS branch returns; early success leaves only private state. Rows may alias because board is read-only. The Solution object retains no state.
numeric: Coordinates and offsets are bounded by R, C and L, and R * C is an exact safe integer. ASCII letters have equal character-index semantics in both languages. All integer inputs and computed mathematical counts (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain within [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. No bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(R * C * 4^L + R + 1) worst-case time, with O(1) early return for empty word. O(R * C + R + L + 1) auxiliary space: private visited rows and an explicit DFS stack with a constant number of pending records per path depth. No recursion or input copy is hidden. Bounds use bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time array indexing and amortized append/pop; output and built-in allocation costs are included.

helpers.name: cardinalNeighbors
helpers.contract: Yields exactly the in-bounds cardinal neighbors in up/right/down/left order, never the current cell or diagonal cells. All coordinate pairs are local.
